question: Does a single SGD update in a nonlinear neural network affect predictions primarily on nearby or semantically similar inputs, and can those update-induced changes serve as a learned similarity for clustering?

key_findings.claim: The paper defines local elasticity through the cross-input effect of one SGD update rather than through a static representation distance.
key_findings.evidence: After updating parameters on labeled point x, a classifier is locally elastic when the prediction change at x' is large for similar x,x' and small for dissimilar points, with a gradual decay. The relative score divides the change at x' by the self-change at x and is parameter-state dependent and asymmetric.

key_findings.claim: A first-order update connects the proposed kernelized similarity to gradient inner products and hence a finite-network tangent kernel.
key_findings.evidence: For small learning rate, the change at x' is approximated by the product of the loss derivative and the inner product between parameter gradients at x and x'. Dividing out the update-specific factor yields S_ker, which equals an NTK-style quantity for the current weights rather than necessarily the fixed infinite-width initialization kernel.

key_findings.claim: For a wide two-layer ReLU network, shared activation gates add an input-dependent locality factor absent from the matched linear network.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 4 approximates the relative update by normalized input inner product times the fraction of neurons active at both x and x'. The appendix derivation assumes normal initialization, a small update, and that only a vanishing fraction of gates switch.

key_findings.claim: Synthetic manifolds show strong monotone relations between geodesic distance and update influence for nonlinear, but not matched linear, networks.
key_findings.evidence: On the torus and folded-box examples, reported correlations are -0.97 and -0.92 for nonlinear networks versus -0.48 and -0.14 for linear versions; additional cosine, helix, cycle, sphere, and sigmoid examples show similar qualitative patterns.

key_findings.claim: The ImageNet probe supports semantic locality in a pretrained network, but is a small selected comparison rather than a population-wide validation.
key_findings.evidence: Across 50 tabby-cat updates, average prediction changes on 25 tiger cats exceed those on 25 warplanes with Wilcoxon p=0.0007; one illustrated update gives KL changes 0.03 versus 0.002. Only these selected synsets and one pretrained ResNet-152 setup are tested.

key_findings.claim: The clustering algorithm converts update effects into pairwise features but requires a labeled superclass discrimination problem and auxiliary-class choices.
key_findings.evidence: Primary examples all share a known superclass label and auxiliary examples receive the opposite label; the model is warmed up on that binary task, updates each primary point, records prediction changes on all primary points, symmetrizes the matrix, and applies K-means or kernel K-means. This is not fully label-free clustering from an undifferentiated dataset.

key_findings.claim: Clustering improvements are substantial on selected MNIST pairs but modest and inconsistent on CIFAR-10.
key_findings.evidence: For MNIST, nonlinear L2 variants reach 50.3--89.3% (FNN) and up to 97.6% (CNN) across six hard digit pairs, often above K-means and linear variants. On the six CIFAR-10 pairs, best displayed nonlinear results are mostly 51--63%, only modestly above chance and baselines.

key_findings.claim: Initialization, architecture, loss, normalization, and auxiliary classes can dominate the observed clustering result.
key_findings.evidence: Near-optimal warm-start weights beat random weights; changing auxiliary digits can reduce the 5-vs-8 result from 75.9% to near chance; the shallow ResNet underperforms CNN; BCE variants often fail; and removing input normalization removes major gains. The paper acknowledges that a rigorous definition and foundation remain future work.

method.core_idea: Use the instantaneous propagation of an SGD update from one input to other inputs as a data-adaptive, training-state-dependent notion of similarity.
method.mechanism: Warm-start a nonlinear classifier on a binary primary-versus-auxiliary task; for each primary example, take an SGD step and evaluate all primary predictions before and after; normalize changes by the self-change or loss derivative; repeat and average if desired; symmetrize the matrix; cluster its rows with K-means or treat it as a kernel for kernel K-means.
assumptions: Semantic or manifold proximity causes shared nonlinear activation/gradient patterns
A one-step prediction change is measurable and larger than numerical noise
The self-change denominator in relative similarity is nonzero and stable
Small-step linearization is accurate for kernelized similarity
Warm-start training learns a representation useful for the unknown subclasses
Chosen auxiliary examples sharpen rather than confound the target subclass structure
Symmetrization yields a useful similarity even though individual update effects are directional

techniques.role: Measures how training on one point perturbs predictions at every other point.
Normalizes cross-input influence by the updating point's self-effect.
Approximates update influence with a parameter-gradient inner product.
Explains ReLU locality through jointly active hidden units.
Aggregates SGD-induced pairwise scores over primary examples and epochs.
Uses an external labeled class to learn features before subclass clustering.

evaluations.setting: torus and folded-box synthetic manifolds with matched nonlinear and linear networks
evaluations.metric: correlation between geodesic distance and relative prediction change
evaluations.result: nonlinear correlations -0.97 and -0.92 versus linear -0.48 and -0.14

evaluations.setting: additional cosine, double-helix, cycle, sphere, and sigmoid synthetic tasks
evaluations.result: qualitative monotone locality persists across the displayed nonlinear examples; activation similarity has -0.97 correlation with Euclidean distance on the torus

evaluations.setting: pretrained ResNet-152 with tabby-cat SGD updates
evaluations.metric: KL prediction change on tiger-cat versus warplane images
evaluations.result: larger changes for tiger cats across 50 updates, Wilcoxon p=0.0007

evaluations.setting: six selected hard MNIST binary subclass pairs, 1,000 primary and 1,000 auxiliary examples
evaluations.metric: cluster accuracy after optimal label permutation
evaluations.result: best nonlinear methods generally exceed K-means/linear baselines, ranging from near chance to 97.6% depending on pair and architecture
evaluations.baseline: K-means, PCA+K-means, matched linear networks, autoencoder, and pretrained ResNet-152 features

evaluations.result: best nonlinear rows yield approximately 51--63%, with small and inconsistent gains over chance and baselines
evaluations.baseline: K-means, PCA+K-means, and matched linear architectures

evaluations.metric: cluster accuracy across initialization, auxiliary classes, normalization, loss, and architecture
evaluations.result: performance varies sharply; warm starts and normalization help, selected auxiliary classes are crucial, and BCE or the tested ResNet often underperform
evaluations.baseline: random initialization, alternative auxiliaries, unnormalized data, and linear models

limitations: The paper explicitly leaves a rigorous mathematical definition and general occurrence theorem open.
Relative similarity is asymmetric and can explode when the updating point's prediction change is small.
Kernelized similarity relies on a small-step first-order approximation; ReLU gate changes create omitted terms.
The clustering procedure uses known primary/auxiliary superclass labels and carefully selected auxiliary examples.
Experiments select six difficult pairs rather than evaluating full multiclass unsupervised clustering.
No repeated-trial uncertainty or confidence intervals are reported for the clustering tables.
CIFAR-10 improvements are weak, and the tested ResNet and BCE configurations often fail.
The main FNN has 40,960 hidden units, making all-pairs update evaluation computationally heavy.
Semantic similarity is asserted through selected examples without a task-independent ground-truth metric.
Local one-step influence is not shown to imply stability, memorization, or generalization; those sections are speculative.
failure_modes: A near-zero self-update denominator produces an extreme relative score unrelated to similarity.
Large learning rates or gate switching invalidate the tangent approximation.
An auxiliary class emphasizes nuisance features and destroys the desired subclass geometry.
Warm-up training memorizes the binary superclass task without learning the hidden subclasses.
The update matrix is indefinite or asymmetric; ad hoc symmetrization can erase directional information.
High within-class semantic diversity makes same-class update influence weaker than cross-class visual similarity.
Batch normalization, dropout, or optimizer state makes a one-example perturbation depend on context rather than input similarity.
All-pairs prediction recomputation becomes quadratic in primary-set size.
A favorable clustering score reflects hand-picked pairs or label permutation rather than general representation quality.
reusable_insights: Training dynamics can define a task-adaptive similarity that static embeddings miss.
Separate directional influence from a symmetric clustering kernel instead of silently conflating them.
Audit update-size normalization and denominator stability when converting influence into similarity.
Auxiliary-task construction is part of the method and must be evaluated as a sensitivity axis.
Compare finite trained tangent kernels with initialization NTKs to measure learned locality.
Use geodesic ground truth on synthetic manifolds to test whether a proposed similarity recovers intrinsic rather than ambient distance.
A scalable version should estimate selected matrix rows or use checkpoint gradients instead of performing every one-point update.
open_questions: Can local elasticity be defined with a metric and probabilistic monotonicity condition that permits exceptions?
What architecture, width, optimizer, and training-phase conditions guarantee local update influence?
Can a stable denominator-free or positive-semidefinite similarity replace the current ratios and symmetrization?
How can auxiliary examples be selected without subclass labels or K-means hindsight?
Does local elasticity predict held-out generalization after controlling for NTK alignment and margins?
Can influence be estimated subquadratically from gradients or randomized sketches?
How does local elasticity behave under label noise, distribution shift, or large minibatches?
Does a dynamic similarity improve full-dataset clustering beyond modern self-supervised embeddings?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Black-box Predictions via Influence Functions
competitive_landscape.difference: Influence functions approximate the effect of infinitesimal upweighting through an inverse Hessian at a fitted solution and target explanations/debugging; local elasticity measures immediate SGD update propagation throughout training and repurposes it as similarity.

competitive_landscape.title: Estimating Training Data Influence by Tracing Gradient Descent
competitive_landscape.difference: TracIn accumulates gradient-dot-product influence over checkpoints where a training example is used and scales to data attribution; local elasticity focuses on spatial/semantic decay of one-step prediction effects and constructs a clustering matrix from them.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Tangent Kernel: Convergence and Generalization in Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.relationship: theoretical kernel foundation for the gradient-inner-product similarity
competitive_landscape.difference: Jacot et al. characterize a deterministic, nearly fixed NTK in the infinite-width limit; this paper emphasizes a finite, trained, data-adaptive tangent similarity whose locality can change with weights and labels.

competitive_landscape.title: Label-Aware Neural Tangent Kernel: Toward Better Generalization and Local Elasticity
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct follow-up that turns local elasticity into a kernel-design objective
competitive_landscape.difference: Label-aware NTK adds supervised Hoeffding-decomposition terms to close the locality/generalization gap between fixed NTKs and networks; this paper introduces the phenomenon and estimates it directly from finite-network SGD updates for clustering.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Nonlinear neural networks exhibit local elasticity under SGD, update-induced prediction changes form useful data-adaptive similarities, and a clustering algorithm built from them supports the phenomenon on synthetic and image data.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper gives two similarity definitions, an activation-overlap calculation, synthetic manifold correlations, an ImageNet semantic probe, MNIST/CIFAR clustering tables, and sensitivity analyses.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The novel lens is valuable: one-step cross-input influence is treated as learned geometry. Evidence is strongest on controlled manifolds and selected MNIST tasks, but the method is not fully unsupervised, is highly configuration-sensitive, and lacks a rigorous or scalable general theory.

reviewer_notes: Read all 19 cached pages, including synthetic definitions, ImageNet/minibatch probes, the gate-switch calculation, and every sensitivity table. Four primary proceedings competitors were checked on PMLR/NeurIPS on 2026-08-23. The reading treats memorization, stability, and normalization claims as proposed implications rather than established consequences and makes the auxiliary-label requirement explicit.
